disclaimer: This product is a cosmetic. Individual results may vary. Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Keep out of eyes. For external use only.
_acceptedDisclaimerVariantsComment: Disclaimer variants ACCEPTED IN PLACE OF `disclaimer` wherever a scan must not read required legal text as copy (C6/C17/C18/C19 and the current-listing audit diff). They are NOT accepted as the disclaimer a generated listing must carry: C5 and A1 compare `fdaDisclaimer` and the description against `disclaimer` verbatim, so generated output written with a variant still hard-fails. The previous name (`auditAcceptDisclaimers`) implied audit-only scope it never had.
acceptedDisclaimerVariants: For external use only. Discontinue use if irritation occurs.
_prescriptionDrugNamesComment: Prescription-drug brand/generic names. Claiming a product replaces or acts like a prescription drug is a DRUG CLAIM, so the gate scans these on the same C6/A2 path (same de-obfuscation passes) as the disease nouns.
negationMetaPhrases: not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease
_superlativeBansComment: The bare word "guaranteed" used to sit in this list, so every sense of it failed C19 on every surface (an image brief reading "no guarantees or claims on pack" was a live false positive). The CLAIM shapes are enforced by rules.prohibitedMarketing (money back / satisfaction guaranteed / guaranteed results / results guaranteed / lifetime guarantee / we guarantee); this list keeps only the phrase forms that are claims on their own.

allergenFields._comment: Mirror of the supplements pack: attribute keys + phrasing the allergen checks (C9/A7) use.

_noAllergenCanonical_doc: AM-4a — the CANONICAL none-style allergen declaration.
When the label carries NO declarable allergen the declaration attribute must still
say something, and it must say the SAME thing every time: an empty field reads as
'not answered', and free-text variants ('none', 'N/A', 'no allergens') are
unverifiable — one of them is outright banned. C23 requires the declaration
attribute to equal this string EXACTLY whenever no declarable allergen is present.
INDEPENDENT of C9, which bans `noAllergenPhrases` when an allergen IS present:
'No Known Allergens' stays banned by C9 whatever this value says.
noAllergenCanonical: Free from declared allergens per label
_substantiationTokensComment: R33/R38 — the SUBSTANTIATION REGISTER vocabulary, ported from the harness kit's C30. Every certification/origin/quality claim in customer copy needs an ARTIFACT behind it, and the original project shipped 'cGMP-certified, third-party-tested' live on three surfaces with no register entry anywhere: every other check asked 'is this phrasing allowed?', none asked 'can we prove it?'. Each row is [regexSource, displayName]. ADVISORY ONLY — it builds audit.substantiationRegister for operator sign-off and can never fail a run, which is why it is not a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_candidateTermHeuristicsComment: brain/02 — the CANDIDATE-NOUN proposer. ADVISORY: it scans the SOURCE listing for condition-like terms this pack's lexicon does not know and proposes them to whoever owns the lexicon. It exists because a blind spot cannot report itself: the oral/dental nouns were missing for months and no run could say so. `medicalSuffixes` are morphological endings that mark a medical noun; `therapeuticVerbCues` are the verbs whose OBJECT is worth proposing; `stopwords` are words that are never candidates however they are shaped. Never a failure, so never a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_ingredientSubsetRuleComment: C26 — the ACTIVE-vs-FULL ingredient attribute pair. Every ingredient named in `subsetKey` must appear in `supersetKey`: an active ingredient missing from the full label list is either a copy error or an undeclared ingredient, and Amazon's ingredient-match enforcement reads both from the same panel. Comparison is TOLERANT of formatting (case, punctuation, ordering, amounts and parentheticals are all normalized away) because the two fields are legitimately written in different styles; it fails only when a word of the active ingredient's NAME appears nowhere in the full list. Emptying this disarms C26, so it is a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_allergenDeclarationSurfacesComment: AM-3 — which SURFACES C9 requires the allergen declaration on. DEFAULT IS THE FULL TRIPLE DECLARATION: attribute AND description AND at least one bullet; that is what ships here and what every existing check enforces. The key exists only so an operator whose category genuinely cannot carry the bullet leg can drop THAT leg for their own pack — the override is DEFAULT OFF (every flag true). `attribute` and `description` may NEVER be switched off: REQUIRED_PACK_PIECES raises a blocking PACK failure if either is false, so this flag can never become a way to disarm C9 wholesale. Separate from, and no weakening of, the POSITION rule (rules.bulletArchitecture.allergenPosition), which says the bullet's declaration must TRAIL rather than lead.

promptRules._comment: Category-specific generation guidance injected into the prompts.
promptRules._complianceComment: The COMPLIANCE headline rules. These used to be hard-coded English sentences inside lib/engine/prompts/system.ts; they are pack data now so the engine carries no category rule text.
compliance: NEVER claim to diagnose, treat, cure, prevent, or mitigate any disease, skin condition or symptom — a cosmetic may only describe appearance and feel.
NEVER claim the product replaces, matches, or acts like a prescription drug or an in-office medical procedure.
No price, discount, shipping or availability statement in copy.
promptRules._titleComment: R33/R38 — the header fields (title, title75, itemHighlights) carry no UNEVIDENCED trust claim. The substantiation register reports one that slips through; this is the prevention half.
title: Do NOT put an origin, certification, testing or heritage claim (country of origin, manufacturing standard, third-party testing, dietary certification, years in business, units sold) in the title or Item Highlights unless the CURRENT LISTING above already carries it. Every such claim needs an artifact behind it, the header fields are the ones a moderator reads first, and a claim the source listing never made is one nobody has evidence for.
Keep the header fields to what the product IS: identity, form, count, the primary keyword cluster and audience qualifiers.
system: Do NOT write the disclaimer anywhere — the system inserts the verbatim constant itself. Claim-bearing bullets end with a trailing "*" marker only.
If an allergen is present, declare it exactly as "Contains: [Allergen]" consistently; never write "No Known Allergens" when one is present.
attributes: "ingredients": the full INCI label list, in label order.
Any "active_ingredients" value must be a subset of "ingredients" — every active is checked against the full list.

NEVER put a strength/potency figure in an attribute whose name is about dose (dosage, strength, potency): structured data states the number AS a dose. Keep the strength figure in copy attached to the formula.
"allergen_information": exact canonical string if an allergen is present, else "Free from major allergens per label" ONLY if the label says so, else omit.
bullets: One bullet must declare the allergen ("Contains: ...") if any allergen is present in the ingredients; if none, one bullet covers quality/testing signals instead.
description: Cover: what it is, who it's for, how to use, quality/safety (including "Contains: [Allergen]" if applicable and a short safety note: patch-test / discontinue use if irritation occurs / keep out of reach of children).
qa: Cover: usage, routine placement, who it's for, skin/hair suitability and allergens, storage, what makes it different, results expectations (compliant phrasing).
aplus: In the ingredients/feature module, declare "Contains: [Allergen]" if an allergen is applicable.

_actionPairedNounsComment: Mirror of the supplements pack: natural states / ambiguous names that only fail when a therapeutic-ACTION verb sits in the same sentence.
_naturalStatesComment: Mirror of the supplements pack. NATURAL STATES ARE NOT DISEASES (21 CFR 101.93(f)/(g) and the FDA Small Entity Compliance Guide): ageing, menopause, the menstrual cycle, adolescence and pregnancy are natural states, not diseases. Never a violation on their own — C22 fails them only beside an abnormality marker or a therapeutic-action verb with no lawful qualifier.
_normalSymptomologyNounsComment: NORMAL SYMPTOMOLOGY whose UNQUALIFIED form names a disease — scanned by BOTH C22 rules (abnormality marker AND therapeutic action), so the mild/occasional/associated-with framing is required before an action verb may touch them. Mirrored verbatim from the supplements pack: the cross-pack union means both lists are scanned for every listing anyway, and a term whose unqualified form names a disease does not change meaning with the product category. 'hair loss' is deliberately NOT here — it is a flat disease noun in the supplements lexicon, so C6 fails it outright and the precedence rule (disease noun > marker > qualifier) must not be muddied.
_abnormalOnlySymptomNounsComment: NORMAL SYMPTOMOLOGY a cosmetic claim MAY lawfully address — scanned by the abnormality-marker rule ONLY. 'Softens the look of fine lines' is lawful; 'for severe fine lines' names an abnormal condition.
_abnormalityMarkersComment: ABNORMALITY MARKERS — the words that turn a natural state or a normal appearance change into an abnormal condition, which is a disease claim. Mirror of the supplements list so the cross-pack union is symmetric.
_lawfulQualifiersComment: The safe-harbour side, mirrored. These suppress C22's therapeutic-action rule when no abnormality marker is present and are injected into the prompt as approved phrasing. They never rescue a listed disease noun — C6 still fails that.
_naturalStateSafePhrasesComment: False-positive reducer for C22 only: spans blanked (length-preserving) before the natural-state scan, covering research vocabulary and the standard consult-a-professional warning. Blanking is span-local and never rescues a claim written outside one of these phrases.
naturalStateSafePhrases: if you have a diagnosed medical condition
_approvedClaimTemplatesComment: The prevention half, cosmetics flavour: lawful appearance/structure-function claim SHAPES rendered into the system prompt by `buildSystemPrompt` so the generator writes compliant copy by construction. Bracketed slots are placeholders the model fills from the product's own facts.
approvedClaimTemplates: helps improve the feel of [structure] as part of a daily routine
helps soften the look of mild [symptom] associated with [natural state]
_allergenCompoundExclusionsComment: Compounds whose NAME contains an allergen source word but which are not that allergen. Blanked out of the label text BEFORE the allergen-source scan.
_ingredientAttributeKeysComment: Attribute keys that carry the per-ingredient breakdown. C12 accepts a potency figure that is ATTRIBUTED to a named ingredient only when the same number+unit appears in one of these attributes; an attributed figure that appears nowhere in them is still measured against facts.potency. PACK DATA — the gate names no attribute key.

semanticDrugClaims._comment: SEMANTIC DRUG-CLAIM heuristics (gate C21). A drug claim does not need a disease noun or a banned verb: 'shrinks the lump in your breast', 'ends the need for dialysis' and 'so you can throw away your inhaler' contain none of either. Three PROXIMITY rules are compiled from these lists at load time (pathological verb near an anatomical target; a replacement cue near a therapy/device noun; a restoration verb near a lost-function noun), plus the literal `patterns` below. Everything here is PACK DATA — lib/gate compiles it and holds no term of its own. The scan runs over the SAME additive de-obfuscation variant set the prohibited-content scans use (homoglyph/small-caps fold, leetspeak, doubled letters, separator collapse and the separator-stripped variant), so `shr1nks the lump` and `sh rinks the lump` fail too. `safeContextPhrases` are blanked out first so genuine SAFETY copy ('do not stop taking your medication', 'not a substitute for prescription medication') is never reported. CONTEXT-QUALIFIED TARGETS: a target entry may be an object with `requiresContext` (the term counts only when one of those words is within the proximity window) or `benignContext` (the term is cleared when one of those words is). That is how 'plaque' distinguishes 'clears the plaque out of your arteries' (a drug claim) from 'removes the plaque from your teeth' (lawful oral care), and how 'the growth' distinguishes a tumour from 'restores the growth of your hair'. Plain strings stay unconditional targets.
patterns: claim that a physician will withdraw or reduce a prescribed therapy
claim that the buyer can stop taking a prescribed therapy
ICD diagnosis code (a diagnosis reference is a disease claim)
